AboutPage.metaDescription: Background and working style of Ahmad Hidayatullah, Information Systems student and developer.
AboutPage.label: About
AboutPage.title: About me
AboutPage.intro: Information Systems student at Gunadarma University, building web and Android apps since 2025.
AboutPage.backgroundText: I started with the web because it was the fastest way to see something I built being used by someone who wasn't me. Android came later, when I wanted to understand what happens when there is no server to fall back on. Both pushed me toward the same habit: decide what the data looks like before writing any UI.
AboutPage.philosophyText: I start with the simplest thing that works. Most of the complexity I've had to undo in my own projects came from solving a problem I didn't have yet.
AboutPage.principle1Title: Let the types do the checking
AboutPage.principle1Desc: TypeScript and Kotlin let me state a rule once instead of re-checking it in every function. I lean on that before reaching for a pattern.
AboutPage.principle2Desc: Server components, incremental static regeneration, and correctly sized images get most of the way there without a performance sprint at the end.
AboutPage.principle3Title: Built around how it gets used
AboutPage.principle3Desc: Mother's focus timer runs as a foreground service, because a study timer that stops when the screen turns off is no use to anyone.
AboutPage.workflowText: Roughly the same loop on every project.
AboutPage.workflowStep1: Talk through what the person actually needs, which is usually narrower than the first request.
AboutPage.workflowStep2: Model the data first: tables, relations, and who is allowed to read what.
AboutPage.workflowStep3: Build it, using types as the contract between layers.
AboutPage.workflowStep4: Test on a real phone and a slow connection, not just on my laptop.
AboutPage.workflowStep5: Ship it, then fix what actually breaks.
AboutPage.goalsText: A part-time internship or freelance projects where I can work alongside more experienced engineers and get my code reviewed properly. I can start now. Full-time has to wait until I graduate, but I would rather learn on a real team than keep building on my own.
